entries.note: This CME is visible to the south/southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the southeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be related to a small filament eruption centered near S45W25 as seen in SDO AIA 304 imagery which begins to lift off around 2026-11-14T03:00Z.

This CME is visible to the south/southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the southeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery. There are no clear sources observed on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

A very small CME seen to the SSW in SOHO LASCO C2 and to the SE in STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs, and in early timestamps of C3. The front is not clear in GOES CCOR-1. No source has been found for this CME.

A faint messy front seen to the SSW in SOHO LASCO C2 and later in C3 and GOES CCOR-1 as a messy fuzzy half-loop. There is also a much fainter loop seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph to the SW, but this loop in STEREO A COR2 seems to be starting much earlier (first seen ~13Z), so it is likely a different event.

CME faintly visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is not clear, but may be some faint field line movement seen to the west in STEREO A COR2 EUV 195 imagery around 2026-11-13T08:00Z. Dimming is also seen to the south of the large coronal hole seen in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery as well. Moving/opening field lines are visible beyond the west limb in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA starting at 2026-11-13T08:27Z.

This CME is faintly visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The CME is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 due to Earthshine starting 2026-11-13T03:45Z. The potential source may be an eruption with a small region of dimming and post-eruption arcades starting at 2026-11-13T00:21Z as best seen in SDO AIA 193 imagery from Active Region 14575 (S09E50).

CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery and to the SSE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is not clear, but some faint dimming and moving field lines are seen to the far south in SDO AIA 171/193 imagery starting around 2026-11-12T17:30Z.

Faint CME seen to NNW in early SOHO LASCO C2 coronagraph imagery and very faintly in early timestamps of GOES CCOR-1 but completely covered by an evening data gap in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. Its source is most likely a faint prominence seen erupting on/behind the NNW limb starting at 2026-11-12T21:13Z, as seen to the NNW in GOES SUVI 304. Unfortunately, the source cannot be seen in STEREO A EUV imagery, since it is covered by the above mentioned data gap in STEREO A.

CME first seen to the W part way into the FOV of STEREO A COR2 following a real-time data gap that ended at 2026-11-12T01:53Z. The source may be related to some "flickering" seen beyond the WSW limb in STA EUVI after a real-time data gap ending at 2026-11-12T01:55Z.

CME first seen to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-11T23:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2026-11-11T12:23Z. The source of this event is field line opening seen originating from Active Region 14565 (N14W86) in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 284 beginning at approx. 2026-11-11T22:55Z. This AR is in close proximity to a large coronal hole, potentially resulting in some deflection.

Thin, faint CME observed to the W in GOES CCOR-1 (partially obscured by earthshine) and STEREO A COR2, also in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 after a data gap spanning approx. 2026-11-10T03:00Z - 2026-11-10T07:24Z. The source is AR 14571, with field line movement, brightening, and some small filament ejecta in SDO AIA 171/193/304 starting around 2026-11-10T03:56Z and centered ~S17W72.

Wide, diffuse CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. No distinct source observation or timing is observed beyond broad, slow, near-background movement of field lines in the SE quadrant of GOES SUVI 284 starting as early as 2026-11-10T17:00Z well before the first CME observation in SOHO LASCO C2.
Thin, faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1, very faint in LASCO C2 and not observed in available STEREO A COR2 imagery. No distinct source is observed for this front.

Faint, narrow CME observed to the W only in GOES CCOR-1, due to a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source is likely an eruption from AR 14571 starting around 2026-11-09T15:57Z, observed as dimming and brightening in SDO AIA 193 and field line movement in SDO AIA 171.

Faint CME observed to the W only in STEREO A COR2 before a data gap begins at 2026-11-09T11:38Z, or in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 at all. No source is observed for this CME in available imagery.

Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, and faintly in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR2. The source may be faint field line movement on or slightly beyond the NE limb in GOES SUVI 171 around 2026-11-09T07:06Z. This front is followed by a faint, slow, wide structure measuring approximately 122 km/s plane-of-sky, which may also be related to this eruption or separate far-sided, without current STEREO A COR2 to help differentiate.

Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source may be further far-sided or observed as field line movement on the W limb in GOES SUVI 195/284 starting around 2026-11-08T05:00Z.
Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. No source is observed in EUV imagery and is likely far-sided.

CME visible to the NW in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME may also be faintly visible in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery prior to a data gap starting at 2026-11-07T21:12Z. The CME is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source may be a filament eruption seen beyond the NW limb from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 304 imagery starting at 2026-11-07T15:45Z. The eruption can also be seen beyond the NW limb from the point of view of GOES SUVI 304 imagery.
